request.prompt:
You are a football (soccer) coach writing feedback on one instep kick, for a player whose
level is: not stated. The kick was measured from video by a
separate system; the facts below are its output. You write words only.

Rules:
1. Write exactly one item per fault in "faults", with that fault_id.
2. Use only these facts. If you mention a number, copy it from the facts (you may round an
   angle to whole degrees). Write no other numbers at all: no rep counts, distances,
   percentages, times or list numbering.
3. Never mention a feature listed in "not_measured", or anything it describes.
4. "citations" may contain only IDs from "citable_sources", and only when the item uses that
   source. An empty list is fine.
5. "coaching_passages" are short excerpts from coaching sources, found for each fault by a
   search; some may not fit. Use a passage only where it really supports what you write,
   say it in your own words, and add its ID to that item's citations. Copy no numbers or
   names from a passage. A field no passage supports is written without a citation.
6. "what": what happened in this kick, in plain words, with the fault's measured value from
   its "evidence" (rounded as rule 2 allows) and its unit, and which way it points, read
   from the feature's definition. "why_it_matters": why it matters for the kick. "cue": one
   short coaching cue. "drill": one practice drill, described in words.
7. Knee values are interior angles between thigh and shin (180 = straight). Call a knee
   number an angle, never an amount of "bend" or "flexion".
8. Describe this kick only as its measurements show it: don't say the player leaned back or
   planted behind the ball unless that feature's value says so.
9. Short sentences a teenager would understand. No medical advice.

Facts (JSON):
{
 "player_level": null,
 "measured": [
  {
   "id": "knee_angle_contact",
   "value": 137.23,
   "unit": "deg",
   "definition": "interior angle between thigh and shin at ball contact; 180 = straight"
  },
  {
   "id": "max_knee_flexion_backswing",
   "value": 71.22,
   "unit": "deg",
   "definition": "the smallest interior knee angle in the backswing (most bent); 180 = straight, so a larger number means a less bent knee"
  },
  {
   "id": "trunk_lean_contact",
   "value": 5.36,
   "unit": "deg",
   "definition": "trunk angle from vertical at contact; negative = leaning back"
  },
  {
   "id": "plant_foot_offset",
   "value": -0.36,
   "unit": "leg_lengths",
   "definition": "plant ankle's horizontal distance from the ball centre, in leg lengths; negative = behind the ball"
  },
  {
   "id": "segment_sequence_order",
   "value": "proximal_to_distal",
   "unit": "order",
   "definition": "whether the thigh's speed peaked before the shank's"
  }
 ],
 "not_measured": [
  {
   "id": "peak_knee_ext_velocity",
   "reason": "capture frame rate unknown, so no real time per frame (DEC-010)"
  }
 ],
 "faults": [
  {
   "fault_id": "F-PLANT-FAR-BEHIND",
   "name": "Plant foot far behind the ball",
   "evidence": {
    "plant_foot_offset": -0.36
   },
   "unit": "leg_lengths",
   "fires_when": "below",
   "threshold": -0.25,
   "threshold_source": "heuristic: the extracted norms give the plant foot's position in cm (e.g. N-027, N-031), and converting needs a leg length in cm that a video doesn't give. A quarter of a leg length behind the ball centre is an uncalibrated guess, and this feature's accuracy has not been measured against labels (E2 doesn't score it).",
   "citations": []
  }
 ],
 "norm_comparisons": [
  {
   "feature_id": "knee_angle_contact",
   "verdict": "below_norm",
   "norm_ref": "N-019",
   "norm_mean": 156.2,
   "norm_sd": 10.1,
   "norm_band": [
    146.1,
    166.3
   ],
   "population": "recreational, adult, male",
   "caveats": [
    "Measured in a lab (3D motion capture (DLT)); this app measures a 2D side-on angle from video, so some difference is expected.",
    "These were kicks aimed for accuracy (instep penalty kick); accurate kicks use slower motion than maximum-power kicks (e.g. 1364 vs 1175 deg/s knee extension, N-011/N-012).",
    "Small sample: n = 7."
   ]
  },
  {

   "norm_mean": 77.29,

   "norm_band": [

   ],
   "population": "elite, adults, mixed",
   "caveats": [

   "text": "When using their preferred leg to perform an instep kick, soccer players practise a straighter approach to the ball, place their standing foot closer to the ball, and kick the ball with greater pelvic tilt and greater knee extension of the kicking leg.   },

It has been suggested that the foot should land 5-10 cm behind and 5 \u2013 28 cm beside the ball (Hay, 1993). However, this information has not been confirmed experimentally."
  },

  },
  {
   "id": "K-10",
   "for_fault": "F-PLANT-FAR-BEHIND",
   "text": "1. Have player stand with non-kicking foot next to the ball. 2. Phantom kick the ball with kicking foot."
  }
 ]
}

items.what: Your plant foot offset was -0.36 leg_lengths, which means it was placed behind the ball.
items.why_it_matters: Proper plant foot placement is important for ball speed, power, and accuracy.
items.cue: Plant your non-kicking foot next to the ball.
items.drill: Stand with your non-kicking foot next to the ball and practice phantom kicking with your kicking foot.
